sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's dive into 2D arrays - they're like spreadsheets for your code! You'll learn how to create and use them like a pro.

• How to declare and initialize 2D arrays
• Accessing elements with row and column indices
• Practical ways to use them in real programs

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a chessboard - that's a perfect real-world example of a 2D array! Each square has a row and column position, just like elements in a 2D array.

A 2D array is simply an array of arrays. Think of it like:
• A grid with rows and columns
• A table where you can store data in organized rows
• A way to represent game boards, images, or spreadsheets

For example, this creates a 3x3 grid:
```java
int[][] grid = new int[3][3];
```
• First number = rows (like floors in a building)
• Second number = columns (like rooms on each floor)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Think of them like spreadsheets or game boards
✓ Use nested loops to process all elements
✓ Rows come first in declaration: new int[rows][columns]
✓ Each row can have different number of columns (jagged arrays)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use descriptive variable names like 'row' and 'col' in loops
Initialize arrays with default values if needed
Check array bounds before accessing elements
donts: Don't forget arrays are 0-indexed (first element is [0][0])
Don't assume all rows have same number of columns
Don't confuse row and column order
sections.protip: Use enhanced for loops for cleaner code when you don't need indices: for(int[] row : matrix) { for(int value : row) { ... } }

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Two-Dimensional Array Basics used in real apps?

examples.how: Each pixel's color values are stored in a 2D array (rows = height, columns = width)
Game boards (chess, tic-tac-toe) and maps use 2D arrays to track positions
Cell values are stored in 2D arrays for quick access and calculations

problem.description:
Create a 3x3 tic-tac-toe board using a 2D array. Write methods to:
1. Initialize the board with empty spaces
2. Place an 'X' or 'O' at a specific position
3. Check if a player has won
hints: Use nested loops to check rows, columns, and diagonals
Remember to validate row and column indices
problem.explanation: The solution initializes a 3x3 board with spaces, places marks safely within bounds, and checks all possible winning combinations (rows, columns, and diagonals).

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 2D arrays store data in rows and columns like a grid
📌 Practice with nested loops to process all elements
📌 You're ready to build game boards and image processors!
